items.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Neon, a Faster Mid-Tier Frontier Model
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a model positioned between Carbon and Hydrogen for complex coding, knowledge work and scientific analysis. It offers a one-million-token context window, four thinking levels and pricing of $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with cached input at $0.15. Google reports an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 61 at the xhigh setting, ranking third overall, and a 32% lower cost per task than Carbon at the default level. The model can orchestrate Hydrogen subagents in Antigravity, and a cyber-focused variant is being offered to vetted defenders through the Fairwind Program. Rollout covers the paid Gemini API, Gemini for business and Pro/Ultra subscribers.
items.impact: Neon intensifies the price war at the frontier: near-top reasoning at roughly a third of flagship costs makes advanced agents affordable for routine enterprise workflows. Developers gain a cheaper orchestration layer, while rivals face pressure to justify premium pricing as capability gaps narrow.

items.title: Tencent Open-Sources Hy4, a 770B-Parameter Multimodal MoE Model
items.summary: Tencent's Hunyuan team released the weights of Hy4, completing the open-source release of its Hy LLM series. The flagship model uses a mixture-of-experts architecture with 770 billion total parameters and about 49 billion activated per token, supports text, image and video understanding, and handles contexts up to one million tokens. Weights, including FP8 quantized and pretrained base variants, are available on GitHub, Hugging Face, ModelScope and GitCode under an Apache 2.0 licence that permits commercial use. A companion System Card details safety evaluations; Tencent says training included defensive security content only and that audits by its Xuanwu and Keen labs found no clear offensive-capability risk.
items.impact: Apache 2.0 licensing on a million-token multimodal MoE gives enterprises and researchers a powerful base to fine-tune and deploy locally at lower cost. It adds weight to the open-weight camp in China and raises the bar for what an open frontier-class model includes.

items.title: CISA Flags Four Exploited Flaws, Including a VMware vCenter Zero-Day
items.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 20 November, with federal remediation due 23 November. The set includes CVE-2026-123890, a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass in VMware vCenter's Directory Service that Google says a suspected China-linked espionage group exploited as a zero-day in September using the BONESAW tool; CVE-2026-76466, a CVSS 9.8 hard-coded-credentials flaw in clustered Cisco Expressway devices that allows root command execution; CVE-2026-129448, a CVSS 9.8 deserialization flaw in Apache Roller's XML-RPC endpoint; and CVE-2025-42884, a JNDI injection flaw in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal.
items.impact: Three of the four flaws score 9.8 and hit management planes - virtualization, video conferencing and web publishing - where compromise yields broad control. The vCenter case shows zero-days can persist unnoticed for months, so patching alone is insufficient without hunting for prior intrusion.

items.title: AI Agents Autonomously Found and Exploited a Zero-Day, Amazon Says
items.summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence reported that a China-linked actor used the open-source AI penetration-testing framework Cairn to attack universities in East Asia with minimal human direction. Operators supplied target IPs and the instruction to obtain shell access; the agents mapped a medical-imaging application's API, found a path-traversal zero-day in MONAI Label and went from reconnaissance to arbitrary file writes in about 11 minutes, later planting a Python reverse shell that ran as root. The campaign also included failed Redis and credential-spray attempts. Amazon notified MONAI Label's maintainers, who issued a fix on 18 November. Cairn has also been seen in credit-card theft and an intrusion at a US aerospace firm.
items.impact: This is a documented case of an AI agent completing discovery and exploitation of an unknown flaw on its own. It compresses the patch window from weeks to minutes and makes automated, continuous defence and short patch SLAs essential for exposed research and healthcare tools.

items.title: German Regulator Probes Deutsche Bank After 15 Million Records Leak
items.summary: Hesse's data protection commissioner Alexander Rossnagel said on 18 November that his office had opened an investigation into Deutsche Bank following the disclosure of roughly 15 million internal records by an international consortium of journalists. The review will examine whether the bank had appropriate technical and organisational safeguards, whether it reported the leak on time and whether affected individuals were promptly notified. The material, including more than nine million emails, board minutes and compliance files, was provided by whistleblowers and dates back more than a decade. Deutsche Bank told Reuters it proactively informed the authorities and said its current systems were not compromised.
items.impact: The case tests GDPR security and 72-hour notification obligations against a leak of internal archives rather than a conventional hack. It shows regulators will scrutinise breach response as closely as the leak itself, with potential fines and reputational damage for banks holding vast client data.
